# Collector rebuild conformance fixture

Entirely synthetic durable harness data. No real transcripts, private paths,
conversation content, credentials, tool payloads, or user artifacts. JSONL keeps
only harness-native metadata and usage fields; OpenCode SQLite is materialized
from reviewable SQL. This fixture exercises the **current** production adapters,
raw persistence, normalization, and canonical identities. It does not implement
or simulate the proposed server ingestion endpoint.

The hand-authored oracle contains 12 countable facts in
[`expected/canonical_facts.json`](expected/canonical_facts.json). Equal token
values do not imply equal requests. Eight facts have components
`90 input + 15 output + 5 reasoning + 10 cache read = 120`. Three have
`20 + 7 + 3 + 4 + 2 = 36`. The Codex child has `20 + 7 + 3 + 4 = 34`.
Aggregate components and total **1102** are independently listed in
[`expected/totals.json`](expected/totals.json).

Codex's expected message strings pin source turn and source time, with the
snapshot hash suffix checked for length. Full actual fact, session, and message
semantic keys, native message strings, and canonical occurrence times are
compared across each rebuild. Internal SQLite row IDs are deliberately excluded.
No expected outputs are generated by running the implementation.

Root `pnpm run test` also checks raw source/stage privacy in
`tools/build/test/fixture-safety.test.ts`: allowlisted metadata, synthetic labels,
no transcript/secret fields, and in-memory OpenCode SQL row inspection.

| Scenario | Executable test | Guarantee / source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CFI-001 | `TestCollectorRebuildFixture` | Exact per-fact components, native references, countability, provider provenance, totals. OpenCode V1/V2 overlap counts once. Pi repeated entry counts once. Claude partial/final/repeated final counts once. Codex duplicate/stale cumulative snapshots are suppressed and verified child replay resolves to original parent facts. Diagnostics required for the latter. |
| CFI-002 | `TestCollectorRebuildRepeatedSyncPreservesFactsAndIdentities` | 100 forced full-refresh parses at advancing clocks preserve fact values and all canonical semantic references. |
| CFI-003 | `TestCollectorRebuildFreshDatabaseAtDifferentClocks` | Two empty replacement databases, earlier/later clocks: same normalized values, semantic references, and occurrence times. No local markers copied. |
| CFI-004 | `TestCollectorRebuildNormalizeRetainedRawWithoutSources` | Clear canonical state, remove every durable source, normalize retained local raw facts at another clock: exact facts/identities recovered. |
| CFI-005 | `TestCollectorRebuildMovingArtifactsPreservesFacts` | Relocate source root; rename/rehouse Pi, Claude, and Codex parent artifacts. Existing and empty replacement databases reproduce exact facts/identities. |
| CFI-006 | `TestCollectorRebuildCopiedArtifactsDoNotMultiplyUsage` | Simultaneous Pi/Claude artifact copies do not multiply usage, including an empty DB rebuild. Codex fork replay is covered by CFI-001. |
| CFI-007 | `TestCollectorRebuildOpenCodeEqualTimestampDistinctNativeRequests` | Two independent native IDs with identical timestamps/counters remain separate; same-ID V1/V2 overlap remains one. Pass: 3 OpenCode facts / 276 tokens. `stages/opencode-equal-time.sql`. |
| CFI-008 | `TestCollectorRebuildClaudeAppendMatchesFreshFinalParse` | Sync partial streaming artifact, then completed artifact. Pass: exactly one completed request / 120 tokens and identical canonical fact identity to a fresh final parse. Session/message occurrence envelopes may retain earlier source history. `stages/claude-partial.jsonl`, `stages/claude-complete.jsonl`. |
| CFI-009 | `TestCollectorRebuildPiMissingIDsRetainRawEvidence` | Both source records are retained locally with missing-message-ID diagnostics. `stages/pi-missing-message-ids.jsonl`. Canonical fallback/counting policy remains pending; different counters cannot establish distinct requests. |

Run from `packages/cli`:

```sh
go test ./internal/pipeline -run '^TestCollectorRebuild' -count=1
```

CFI-007–008 intentionally assert correct accounting and currently fail. They are
not skipped or quarantined. Fixes must preserve the hand-authored oracle rather
than update expected counts to match data loss/duplication.

## Limits

CFI-003 is the unchanged-input reconstruction guarantee. CFI-008 tests **changed
input across syncs**; it is not evidence that parsing identical source bytes in
empty databases is nondeterministic. Both matter before publishing canonical
facts to a server that retains previous uploads.

CFI-009 preserves an adversarial weak-identity input and verifies raw capture and
diagnostics only. Its two records have different counters but no native message
IDs; they may represent independent requests or revisions of one request. An
initial assertion requiring two canonical contributions was rejected by independent
review because that identity policy is unresolved. The canonical collision remains
an audit finding, not a passing claim or an approved fallback rule. A future test
must require either justified distinct identities or explicit ambiguity handling.

The suite covers file movement with retained native session identities; it does
not promise stability when those identities are absent or when identity rules
change incompatibly. Copied Codex parent files can make ancestry ambiguous and
are intentionally outside CFI-006's claim; ancestry ambiguity, missing parents,
and cycles have separate existing Codex conformance tests.

Crash/commit boundaries, HTTP retry, batch receipt persistence, schema negotiation,
delivery cursors, and concurrent server ingestion need tests against the future
production collector journal and server implementation. Passing this suite alone
cannot establish those guarantees. See the proposed
[failure contract](../../../../../docs/collector-ingestion-tests.md).
